 Order
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

2. This is an application for bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner in anticipation of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s.376(2)(1)/506 of IPC and in connection with Bari Ramachandrapur PS Case No.318 of 2022 corresponding to CT Case No.2283 of 2023 pending in the court of learned SDJM, Jajpur.
3. It is alleged that the Petitioner by alluring the victim who is allegedly to be a mentally retarded girl was subjected to rape on many occasions leading to her pregnancy.

On being asked to the victim,
she identified the present Petitioner being the person who who deed the carnal act.
The medical examination report too substantiated the victim to be a pregnant.

Mr. D. Nayak, Learned Sr. Counsel for the Petitioner submits that the alleged act cannot be brought under Section 376(2)(1) of IPC and the victim being mentally not sound, the above statement of the victim allegedly identifying the present Petitioner to be the person responsible to Pabitra Mohan Jena vs State Of Odisha .... 1 get her impregnated cannot be prima-facie accepted as true.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State submits that the overall circumstances clearly points to the Petitioner as the culprit.
The statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 CrPC substantially implicates the present Petitioner as specifically identified by the victim.

6. Keeping in view the nature of allegations as emerged from the materials on record, the circumstances appearing, the seriousness and gravity of the offences, this court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner.
The prayer for bail accordingly stands rejected and the ABLAPL is dismissed.
(Chittaranjan Dash) Judge AKPradhan Signed by: ANANTA KUMAR PRADHAN
